annotation.title_clean: The future scope of leadership artificial intelligence smart electronics device based legal robotics industries
annotation.title_en: The future scope of leadership artificial intelligence smart electronics device based legal robotics industries
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Vinodh, N.; Subramani, A.K.; Neeraja, P.; Shoba, K.B.
annotation.venue: International Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences
annotation.summary_en: Indian journal article on AI and robotics in the legal sector, discussing legal challenges around liability, privacy, intellectual property, cybersecurity and robot legal personhood. It notes India has no law recognising AI as legal persons and suggests new regulatory measures. Mostly concerns AI legal tools rather than physical robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: India currently has no laws recognising AI entities as legal persons.
Traditional legal norms inadequately address autonomous, self-learning robots; new legal frameworks are needed.
Liability for AI errors usually falls on the user, or on the developer or manufacturer if the fault is in design or programming.
Strict liability for service robots must be balanced against the risk of deterring investment.
AI in legal practice raises privacy, cybersecurity and accountability concerns; it should assist rather than replace lawyers.
